name: Dedalus Labs

plans.name: Hobby
plans.note: 50 active compute-hours/month ceiling (hard free-plan limit); 10 GiB storage per machine hard cap; up to 4 vCPU / 16 GiB per machine; up to 5 machines.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: $20 monthly compute credit, refreshes each cycle, does not roll over (purchased credits do roll over). Configurable timeout; unlimited compute; up to 16 vCPU / 64 GiB, 20 machines.

free.notes: Startup program: up to $10,000 compute credits valid 12 months for qualifying startups.

caveats: Cloud Hypervisor-derived custom VMM; CPU/RAM charged per second while actively running, idle sleep free. This is lifecycle-active, not proven CPU-utilization billing.

Storage headline incorrectly labels $0.073 as per GiB-hour; calculator/FAQ explicitly use $0.0001/GiB-hour ($0.073 at 730h). Use FAQ and preserve conflict. Unlimited Pro storage means capacity, not free bytes.

Hobby 5 machines and 50 compute-hours/month; Pro 20 machines. Fifty concurrent requires Enterprise, whose fee and rates are unknown. Pricing footer says join waitlist: public rates do not prove instant admission.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.
SSH verified 2026-09-28: skill docs say "Use dedalus ssh $MACHINE_ID for an interactive shell" (https://docs.dedaluslabs.ai/.well-known/skills/dedalus-machines/skill.md).
Lifecycle mutations are rate limited (RATE_LIMITED, scope mutating_lifecycle_routes, retry_after_ms) with no published numeric limit.
SSH sessions close after 30 idle minutes or 12 hours total; deleted machines' storage may be retained up to 30 days.

Autosleep default is 300 idle seconds ('Machines sleep after five minutes of inactivity by default'); pricing says 'Idle time is free' and billing is for active compute, but docs say compute billing stops on sleep. Whether the up-to-5-minute idle tail before autosleep is billed is not stated.

fleet.verification: Hobby says no credit card; beta organization grant required.
fleet.notes: Machine creation also requires DCS beta admission; authenticated API access alone does not prove eligibility. A BETA_ACCESS_REQUIRED response needs support to check the org grant. 50/300/1,000 are not published self-serve allowances. Machine count is a published provisioning allowance; docs and footer also advertise waitlist access.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Only the root filesystem survives sleep and wake.
snapshot_auto.note: Docs list what is lost on every sleep: 'RAM, running processes, vCPU state'. Autosleep (default 300 idle s) stops the VM; only the persistent root disk survives (that is persistent_disk, not a snapshot). Pricing FAQ mentions 'observed logical storage snapshots' but only as the storage-billing measurement method.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: You can create a Machine, run non-interactive commands, open a temporary Secure Shell (SSH) session, change its resources, put it to sleep, and wake it later with its root filesystem intact.
snapshot_on_demand.note: The complete public OpenAPI (https://docs.dedaluslabs.ai/dcs-openapi.json: machines, executions, SSH, artifacts, usage; ops create/update/sleep/wake/reboot/delete) and CLI command index have no snapshot/checkpoint/fork/template/image operation; CreateMachineRequest only takes vcpu, memory_mib, storage_gib, autosleep.

harness_api.quote: An execution runs one non-interactive command inside one Machine. Create returns an `execution_id`.
harness_api.note: Only a generic exec API (executions with events/output) plus SSH; no Claude Code/Codex/agent-session API. The 'agent skill' is a SKILL.md that teaches an outside coding agent to drive the CLI, not an in-sandbox harness API.

ingress_rules.quote: no network-facing surface exposed by default — machines get private IPs and don't accept inbound connections directly.
ingress_rules.note: No port exposure / preview URL feature at all, so no ingress controls to configure: machines are private-only; reach them through authenticated, temporary SSH sessions (CLI does SSH port forwards). Not 'every port public', but no public exposure option either.

guest_firewall.note: Full VM with its own guest kernel and root (custom Cloud Hypervisor fork), so nftables/iptables inside should work; not documented.

secret_proxy.note: Only mechanism to pass secrets is env vars per execution (CreateExecutionRequest.env). Dedalus Auth (DAuth, https://www.dedaluslabs.ai/blog/dedalus-auth-launch) is a separate MCP-server credential enclave product, not an outbound-request proxy for Machines.

volume_attach.quote: Persistent storage allocated to the machine, measured in gibibytes (GiB).
volume_attach.note: Only a resizable per-machine root disk (storage_gib); no volume resources in the OpenAPI or endpoint catalog.

volume_shared.quote: Persistent storage allocated to the machine, measured in gibibytes (GiB).
volume_shared.note: Storage is per machine; no shared filesystem/volume feature in API or docs (storage is 'disaggregated from compute' internally, but not shareable).
